title: Rapid mixing of Glauber dynamics with \(\Delta +2\) colours
formal: Are there absolute constants \(C,c>0\) such that for every finite simple undirected graph \(G\) with \(n\ge1\) vertices and maximum degree \(\Delta\), and every integer \(q\ge\Delta+2\), the single-vertex heat-bath Glauber chain on proper labelled \(q\)-colourings satisfies \[t_{\mathrm{mix}}(1/4)\le Cn^c?\] The constants must be independent of the graph, its degree and the number of colours. This retains the previously selected degree-uniform polynomial target; the time unit is one vertex update, not a sweep or a bit operation.
definitions:
Let \(V(G)=[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and let \(E(G)\) be a set of unordered pairs of distinct vertices. There are no loops or parallel edges. Set \(N_G(v)=\{u:\{u,v\}\in E(G)\}\) and \(\Delta=\max_v|N_G(v)|\). The state space is \[\Omega_{G,q}=\{\sigma:[n]\to[q]:\sigma(u)\ne\sigma(v)\text{ for every }\{u,v\}\in E(G)\},\] where \([q]=\{1,\ldots,q\}\). Colours are labelled and may be unused. There is no constraint on colour-class sizes, and no prescribed partial colouring or vertex-specific list. The state space is nonempty for the stated colour range.

At each discrete step, choose \(v\) uniformly from \([n]\). Given the current state \(\sigma\), form the available set \[A_\sigma(v)=[q]\setminus\{\sigma(u):u\in N_G(v)\}.\] Choose a colour uniformly from \(A_\sigma(v)\), assign it to \(v\), and leave every other vertex unchanged. The set has at least \(q-\Delta\ge2\) elements and includes the current colour; staying in the same colouring is allowed. The choices at successive steps are made from these conditional distributions. Let \(P\) be the resulting finite stochastic matrix and let \(P^t(\sigma,\tau)\) be its \(t\)-step transition probabilities, with \(P^0\) the identity matrix. The chain is reversible with respect to \(\pi(\sigma)=1/|\Omega_{G,q}|\), the uniform law on all proper labelled colourings. In this range it is irreducible and has self-loops, so that this stationary law is approached from every state.

For probability laws \(\mu,\nu\) on the finite state space, total variation is \(d_{\mathrm{TV}}(\mu,\nu)=\frac12\sum_{\tau\in\Omega_{G,q}}|\mu(\tau)-\nu(\tau)|\). Define \[t_{\mathrm{mix}}(1/4)=\min\left\{t\in\mathbb N_0:\max_{\sigma\in\Omega_{G,q}}\frac12\sum_{\tau\in\Omega_{G,q}}|P^t(\sigma,\tau)-\pi(\tau)|\le\frac14\right\}.\] One may set this minimum to infinity if the set is empty; ergodicity in the stated range ensures that it is finite. The maximum is over arbitrary initial proper colourings, with no warm-start or random-initial-state assumption.

A step updates one vertex. No factor of \(n\) is absorbed into the time unit, and uniform sampling from a potentially large colour set is part of the mathematical transition rule. Thus the statement concerns the convergence rate of a specified chain, not an implementation bound polynomial only in \(n\) for operations on \(\log q\)-bit colour names. If a graph is encoded for formalization, use its explicit vertex and edge lists and the binary integer \(q\); no succinct graph representation is intended.

The bound is simultaneous for all finite degrees and all \(q\ge\Delta+2\), including \(q\) unbounded as a function of \(n\). A theorem of the form \(C_{\Delta,q}n^{c_{\Delta,q}}\) for each fixed pair of parameters does not automatically meet it. No girth, treewidth, chordality, planarity, expansion or random-graph assumption is imposed. Girth is the shortest cycle length, with infinity for a forest. A fixed multiplicative slack \(q\ge(1+\delta)\Delta\), with \(\delta>0\), does not cover \(q=\Delta+2\) uniformly as \(\Delta\) increases.

The heat-bath convention differs from proposing a uniformly random colour from all \([q]\) and rejecting a conflict, often also called Glauber or Metropolis dynamics. In the heat-bath chain, every proposed colour is available; in the latter chain, unsuccessful proposals contribute further holding probability. Flip dynamics can recolour an entire two-colour component and is a third chain. Related results must retain their update convention and comparison costs. The present question fixes the heat-bath chain exactly.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of the displayed uniform polynomial bound, or a complete Lean-checked proof of its failure. An affirmative proof must supply absolute \(C,c\) working for every graph, degree, colour count and initial proper colouring in the definition. A negative answer must show that for every proposed \(C,c\) there are eligible \(n,G,q\) with \(t_{\mathrm{mix}}(1/4)>Cn^c\); one slow instance does not refute every polynomial. Polynomial mixing only for each fixed degree with an uncontrolled exponent, larger multiplicative palette slack, restricted graphs, a different dynamics, or an unspecified faster sampler is not the required bound. This is an exact asymptotic proposition about the specified chain, not a request to approximate a finite mixing time to the numerical benchmark tolerance.
why: This tests whether the simplest local update rule samples proper colourings efficiently throughout the full range where it is guaranteed to move between all solutions. It connects random sampling, approximate counting and antiferromagnetic spin systems at a longstanding boundary for general graphs.

importance.reason: A longstanding general-graph conjecture linking local algorithms, approximate counting and spin systems; recent near-threshold results still require structural restrictions.

progress.text: The primary source states the additive-threshold conjecture and proves bounded-treewidth and slack-dependent chordal special cases.
The flip-dynamics theorem improves the general-graph palette ratio to1.809 for Δ≥125, with explicitly qualified Glauber consequences.
The ICALP paper reiterates the ordinary uniform-colouring conjecture while developing separate prescribed-class-size samplers.
A preprint gives heat-bath rapid mixing at fixed relative slack on sufficiently high-degree graphs of girth at least five.
The revised Metropolis paper reaches girth seven with fixed relative slack and a slack-dependent degree threshold.

On16September2026 the original full Conjecture1 and chain definition, the ICALP2026 repeated conjecture, the2024 full Theorem1.1/Corollary1.2, and the August2026 girth-seven and girth-five definitions/main theorems were checked with current version metadata. context_blocks.text: The source poses polynomial mixing at the degree-plus-two threshold. This card retains the already adopted heat-bath update rule and the explicit requirement of one polynomial for all degrees and palettes. The source’s initial update description uses proposal-and-rejection; that clock is stated separately rather than silently identifying its transition matrix with this one.

At one fewer colour, a clique on Δ+1 vertices can be frozen: every vertex already sees every other colour. Thus ergodicity itself can fail at q=Δ+1. At q≥Δ+2 the basic chain is ergodic, but eventual convergence alone supplies no polynomial bound on how long it takes.

The2020 source proves polynomial mixing for bounded-treewidth graphs at the additive threshold and for chordal graphs with fixed multiplicative slack. Its treewidth-dependent exponent and the extra hypotheses do not establish the all-graph uniform statement.

The2024 flip-dynamics theorem applies for Δ≥125 and q≥1.809Δ. Its comparison gives polynomial Glauber mixing in that range; the sharper O(n log n) corollary permits a constant depending on degree and palette. Neither the larger palette ratio nor that parameter dependence is the selected degree-plus-two theorem.

The August2026 girth-seven revision treats Metropolis updates with q≥(1+δ)Δ, for fixed δ and degree sufficiently large in terms of δ. The separate girth-five preprint gives a heat-bath theorem under analogous fixed-slack and large-degree conditions. The latter’s general bound is Oδ(n² log q+n log(1/ε)); its optimal-order corollary has further bounded-degree qualifications. Both retain structural assumptions absent here.

The ICALP2026 paper repeats the ordinary colouring-sampling conjecture before studying prescribed colour-class sizes. Fixing class sizes changes the stationary state space and the allowed moves, so those refined sampling results do not settle the chain defined here.

sentences: The question concerns a local Markov chain that recolours one vertex uniformly from its currently available colours.
It asks for one polynomial mixing bound for every graph and every palette with at least two more colours than the maximum degree.
The stationary law is uniform on all proper labelled colourings and the bound must hold from the worst initial colouring.
Known general-graph and recent near-threshold results retain larger palette slack, structural assumptions or parameter-dependent qualifications.
Resolving the uniform additive-threshold conjecture would clarify the power of elementary local sampling for constrained spin systems.
